finding_F30_PRICE_HONESTY_COMMITMENT.claim: Google Flights publishes an explicit all-in pricing commitment — the stated opposite of drip pricing.
finding_F30_PRICE_HONESTY_COMMITMENT.evidence_verbatim: Prices are final prices and include all taxes and fees, including payment fees for the cheapest common payment method (which may d[iffer]...)
finding_F30_PRICE_HONESTY_COMMITMENT.contrast: Expedia disclosed city tax per person per night at the property page — good, but late and per-item. Booking.com said only 'Includes taxes and fees'. Google states a platform-level commitment BEFORE any search, and names the payment-fee edge case rather than hiding it.
finding_F30_PRICE_HONESTY_COMMITMENT.why_it_matters: For a first-time traveller the fear is not the headline price, it is what appears at the end. A stated all-in commitment answers that fear before it forms.

finding_F31_BUILT_FOR_THE_UNDECIDED.claim: Google Flights explicitly addresses a traveller who has not decided, in its own copy.
evidence_verbatim: Not ready to book yet? Observe price changes for a route or flight and get notified when prices drop.
If your travel plans are flexible, use the form above... then play around with the Date grid
finding_F31_BUILT_FOR_THE_UNDECIDED.why_it_matters: Booking.com and Expedia both REQUIRE destination and dates as search inputs — an undecided traveller cannot start. Google treats indecision as the normal starting state and builds tools for it: date grid, price graph, price history, tracking. This is the scenario's stage 1 'Dream & discover', which the transactional incumbents skip entirely.
finding_F31_BUILT_FOR_THE_UNDECIDED.running_pattern: Reinforces F-26. Across three competitors, decision-support and transaction are inversely distributed. Nobody observed so far holds both.

capability_inventory_flights: Date grid — price across a matrix of departure/return dates
Price graph — price over time for a route
Price insights / price history — is now a good time to book
Price tracking with notification — monitoring while away
Multi-origin search ('Where else?' fields on both from and to)
note_multi_origin: The search form offers 'Where from? / Where else?' and 'Where to? / Where else?' — multiple origins AND multiple destinations in one query. Neither transactional competitor observed offers this.
our_product_decision_required: Decision required: Luma's Core Features list includes 'live flight tracking' — Google already ships price tracking, price history and a date grid, free, without a booking. Luma's flight layer starts behind, not ahead. What does Luma add that Google does not already give away?

Decision required: an all-in price commitment (F-30) is a stated policy, not a feature build. It costs nothing to adopt at ideation and directly answers the target user's core fear. Is it a Luma commitment?

Decision required: every transactional competitor requires dates and destination to begin. Google does not. Luma's stage 1 is 'Dream & discover' — can its search accept an undecided traveller, or does it inherit the incumbents' assumption?

the handoff to airline or OTA after selection
